classification.difficultyReason: Requires expressing opposite angles of the inner quadrilateral through two surrounding triangles and connecting their sum to the halved angle sum of the outer quadrilateral; the half-angle labels are supplied.

content.prompt:
The diagram shows quadrilateral $ABCD$ and the bisectors of the angles at $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$. The bisectors at $A$ and $B$ intersect at the point $P$. The bisectors at $A$ and $D$ meet at $Q$. The bisectors at $C$ and $D$ meet at $R$. The bisectors at $B$ and $C$ meet at $S$.

Show that $PQRS$ is a cyclic quadrilateral.

spec.description: Quadrilateral and its four angle bisectors, with Q below BC and the inner quadrilateral emphasised.
spec.mathematics: P=AP∩BP, Q=AQ∩DQ, R=CR∩DR, S=BS∩CS; each vertex angle has two equal labelled halves.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied angle-half labels are permanent givens; the proof is answer-only.

answer.worked:
Let $\alpha=\frac12\angle A$, $\beta=\frac12\angle B$, $\gamma=\frac12\angle C$ and $\delta=\frac12\angle D$.

The angle sum of quadrilateral $ABCD$ gives
$$\begin{align*}2\alpha+2\beta+2\gamma+2\delta&=360^\circ\\\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta&=180^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Using the angle sums of $\triangle BSC$ and $\triangle AQD$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle PSR&=\angle BSC=180^\circ-(\beta+\gamma)\\\angle PQR&=\angle AQD=180^\circ-(\alpha+\delta).\end{align*}$$
Here $SP$ lies along $SB$ and $SR$ lies along $SC$, while $QP$ lies along $QA$ and $QR$ lies along $QD$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle PSR+\angle PQR&=2\times180^\circ-(\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta)\\\angle PSR+\angle PQR&=2\times180^\circ-180^\circ\\\angle PSR+\angle PQR&=180^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $PQRS$ is cyclic because its opposite angles are supplementary.
